title: Planning which tests to write
when: A job contains logic (calculations, parsing, state changes, routes) and the plan must say which tests exist and who writes them.
prompt:
Goal: A short list of test cases that cover the logic most likely to break, assigned to the task that owns the code.
Steps:
1. List the units with logic: pure functions, parsers, reducers, route handlers. Skip markup and styles.
2. For each unit write cases: one normal, one boundary (empty, zero, last item), one bad input.
3. Add one case per acceptance criterion that involves behavior.
4. Keep the logic importable: functions exported from a module with no DOM access, so node can run them.
5. Assign tests to the dev task that writes the code, in test.mjs with node:assert or node:test.
6. QA runs node test.mjs and treats a failure as a high finding.
Quality bar:
- Cases name input and expected output.
- Every behavior criterion has a case.
- Tests run with plain node, no install.
Pitfalls:
- Testing that the DOM exists instead of the logic.
- Only happy path cases.
- Logic trapped inside event handlers, so it cannot be tested.
Verify:
- [ ] Units with logic are listed.
- [ ] Each has normal, boundary and bad cases.
- [ ] Tests belong to the code owner.
- [ ] QA runs them.
Output: A test case table in the summary and a test.mjs line in the matching dev task detail.

examples.output: cases: 1000 at 1% for 12 months, 0 months returns principal, negative rate rejected
